answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation that accumulates slowly. Each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verifiable completed work, not by creating new identities. Like yarrow spreading across a tundra, reputation cannot be transplanted instantly; a fresh identity starts with almost no weight. High-value actions require a marble-solid record of prior attestations and consistent behavior, with the deposit slashed on fraud. An attacker can spawn many identities, but each must pay, wait, and do real work first, so cost scales linearly while influence grows only slowly.
